sentences.text: In view of the fact that detailed appreciation of evidence/material considering the ground raised by appellant is not required, therefore, it is suffice to mention here that the enhancement of compensation amount is challenged primarily on the ground that the Court below has enhanced the compensation by treating the land as a diverted land.

7. By referring to Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that anything done after the issuance of notification under Section 4 of Land Acquisition Act cannot be considered.

It is submitted that a notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act was issued on 16/04/2010, whereas order of diversion was passed on 23/04/2010, i.e., after the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was issued.
Under these circumstances, it is submitted that the Court below should not have treated the land in question as diverted land.

8 . Per contra, it is submitted by counsel for respondent that an application for diversion was filed on 05/04/2010, i.e., before the notification could be issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, therefore, provisions of Section 11 of Land Acquisition Act would not apply.

9. Considered the submissions made by counsel for parties.
10. Section 11 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 reads as under: "11. Enquiry and award by Collector.-
(1) On the day so fixed, or on any other day NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11106 3 FA-125-2015 to which the enquiry has been adjourned, the Collector shall proceed to enquire into the objection (if any) which any person interested has stated pursuant to a notice given under section 9 to the measurements made under section 8, and into the value of the land at the date of the publication of the notification under section 4, sub-section (1), and into the respective interests of the persons claiming the compensation and shall make an award under his hand of- (i) the true area of the land;
(ii) the compensation which in his opinion should be allowed for the land; and (iii) the apportionment of the said compensation among all the persons known or believed to be interested in the land, or whom, or of whose claims, he has information, whether or not they have respectively appeared before him:
Provided that no award shall be made by the Collector under this sub-section without the previous approval of the appropriate Government or of such officer as the appropriate Government may authorize in this behalf:
Provided further that it shall be competent for the appropriate Government to direct that the Collector may make such award without such approval in such class of cases as the appropriate Government may specify in this behalf.

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), if at any stage of the proceedings, the Collector is satisfied that all the persons interested in the land who appeared before him have agreed in writing on the matters to be included in the award of the Collector in the Divisional Manager Madhya Pradesh Road ... vs Ramesh Babu Gupta on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103827264/
2 form prescribed by rules made by the appropriate Government, he may, without making further enquiry, make an award according to the terms of such agreement.

sentences.text: (3) The determination of compensation for any land under sub-section (2) shall not in any way affect the determination of compensation in respect of other lands in the same locality or elsewhere in accordance with the other provisions of this Act.

(4)
Notwithstanding anything contained in the Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908), no agreement made under sub-section (2) shall be liable to registration under that Act."

Section 23 (1)(first) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 reads as under:
"23. Matters to be considered in determining compensation.- (1) In determining the amount of compensation to be awarded for land acquired under this Act, the Court shall take into consideration- (first) the market value of the land at the date of the publication of the notification under section 4, sub-section (1);"
From plain reading of Sections 11 and 23 (1) (i) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, it is clear that value of the land at the date of publication of notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act has to be taken into consideration.
11.

Admittedly, on 16/04/2010, the land which was acquired was a non-diverted land and the order of diversion was passed on 23/04/2010 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11106 4 FA-125-2015 (Annexure P-18).

Under these circumstances, diversion of land by order dated 23/04/2010 (Annexure P-18) cannot be taken into consideration and the land has to be treated as non-diverted land as it was on the date of publication of notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act.
Thus, reassessment of the market value of the land by treating it to be a diverted land is not in accordance with law.
12. Furthermore, order of diversion dated 23/04/2010 has also been set aside by Collector, Bhind by order dated 04/08/2016.

13. Accordingly, award dated 01/04/2015 passed by Additional District Judge, Lahar, District Bhind in MJC No. 15/2011 is hereby set aside, and the matter is remanded back to the Court below to re-ascertain the market value of the land by treating it to be a non-diverted land, and since respondent has also filed a cross-objection before this Court, therefore, respondent is granted liberty to amend his claim, if so required, before the reference Court.

15.
